chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, you are only a warner, and for every people is a guide' [13:7].
So he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the warner, and Ali is the guide.'
O Abu Muhammad! Is there a guide today? I said: Yes, may I be your sacrifice! There has not ceased to be from among you a guide after a guide until it was handed over to you.

So he said: May God have mercy on you, O Abu Muhammad! Had it been so that a verse was revealed to a man, then that man died, the verse would die, the Book would die. But it is living; it flows among those who remain just as it flowed among those who have passed.

key_terms.حَيٌّ يَجْرِي: Alive and flowing — the Quran's living, dynamic nature as it continues to be applied and interpreted in each era
key_terms.مُنْذِرٌ: Warner — one who delivers warnings; the Imam identifies the Prophet Muhammad as the fulfillment of this role
key_terms.هَادٍ: Guide — one who provides ongoing guidance; the Imam identifies Imam Ali and by extension all Imams as the fulfillment of this role

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Quran being a living text that flows through every generation?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer presents a Quranic verse (13:7) to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who interprets 'the warner' as the Prophet and 'the guide' as Imam Ali (AS), establishing that the Imamate is an ongoing institution. The Imam then articulates a profound principle of Quranic hermeneutics: the Quran is a living text whose meanings are not frozen in history but continue to unfold through every generation, carried by the Imams as living interpreters. This hadith was delivered to Abu Baseer, a trusted companion of the Imam, in what appears to be a private instructional setting.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on you

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour Bin Ismail, from Sa’dan, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘[13:7] But rather, you are only a warner, and for every people is a Guide.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> is the warner, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> the guide’.

O Abu Muhammad! Is there a guide today?’ I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There has not ceased to be from you (Imams<sup>asws</sup>), a guide after a guide until it (Imamate) was handed over to you<sup>asws</sup>’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you<sup>asws</sup>, O Abu Muhammad! Had it been so that a Verse was Revealed unto a man, then that man was to die, the Verse would die, the Book would die. But, it is alive. It flow among the ones<sup>asws</sup> who remain just as it flows among the ones<sup>asws</sup> of the past’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husaym ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Sa‘dan from abu Basir who has said that he asked Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the meaning of the words of Allah. “(Muhammad), you are only a Warner. For every nation there is a guide.” [13:7]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “The Holy Prophet is the Warner and Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) is the guide.

O abu Muhammad, is there a guide today?” I said, “Yes, may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, there has always been a guide from you one after the other until this (noble task) is being carried on by your own self.”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “O abu Muhammad, may Allah grand you blessings. Had it been like the coming of guidance to man and then he would die with his death the guidance would also die and the whole book would die, but it lives and it continues with new generations as it has done so with the people in the past.”
